                    ### Question
                    A 19-year-old college student presents to student health with 1 day of fever and chills. He says that he has also been coughing for 2 days. His roommate was sick 3 days ago with similar symptoms and was diagnosed with Mycoplasma infection. He has otherwise been healthy and has had all the required vaccines as scheduled. He is currently taking introductory biology as part of his premedical studies and recently learned about antibodies. He therefore asks his physician about what his body is doing to fight off the infection. At this stage of his infection, which of the following forms are the antibodies circulating in his serum?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Dimers
opb. Monomers
opc. Pentamers
opd. Tetramers
ope. Trimers

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the early stages of a Mycoplasma infection, the immune system primarily produces IgM antibodies. IgM antibodies are structured as pentamers, consisting of five monomer units. This structural configuration enhances their pathogen-binding efficacy and ability to activate the complement system, crucial for combating the infection. The evidence supports that IgM is the predominant antibody type produced in response to initial Mycoplasma exposure, aligning with the patient's current symptoms and infection timeline.
